q: _viruses are embedded in a system's memory so it can be reactivated if the original virus is deleted.
solution:
The correct answer is Resident.

Key Points

• A computer virus is a type of malevolent code or program written to alter the way a computer operates and is designed to spread from one computer to another.

• A virus is corporate by inserting or attaching itself to a lawful program or document that supports macros in order to execute its code.

• In the procedure, a virus has the prospective to cause unannounced or damaging effects, such as harming the system software by corrupting or destroying data.

• Common types of Computer Viruses are:

• File Infecting Virus

• Macro Virus

• Trojan Horse

• Browser Hijacker

• Web Scripting Virus

• Boot Sector Virus

• Polymorphic Virus

• Resident Virus

• Multipartite Virus​​

Important Points

• Resident Virus:

• ​Resident Viruses is a permanent virus that stays in the RAM memory and could cause interruption of the operations that the system has executed.

• This leads to corrupt files and programs.

• Examples are CMJ, Mr Klunky, Randex, and Meve.

• ​Trojan Horse:

• ​A Trojan horse is a hidden piece of code. Viruses enter a system secretly where the Trojan horse enters by deceiving a user.

• A user allows or invites a Trojan into the system, believing in it, but actually, the Trojan horse contains some malicious code to perform some malicious activity.

• Before a Trojan can attack, it must find a way to entice the victim to copy, download, and run it.

• Since few people would knowingly run a malicious program, Trojan must disguise themselves as other programs that the victim believes to be harmless (such as games, utilities, or popular applications).

• File Infector:

• ​File infector virus is also known as a parasitic virus that usually infects memory and executable files.

• Multipartite:​

• This virus can attack both the boot sector and executable files of an infected computer.

• When the virus attaches to the boot sector, it will in turn affect the system files.

• When the virus attaches to the files, it will, in turn, infect the boot sector.

q: A  can either be malware or hardware. The main purpose of this malware is to record the keys pressed by a user on the keyboard.
solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

Concept:

Keyloggers, also known as keystroke loggers, are software applications or hardware devices that record the activity (keys tapped) on a keyboard. Keyloggers are a type of spyware in which users are unaware that their actions are being recorded.

Spyware: Spyware is a type of malicious software or malware that is installed on a computing device without the end user's knowledge.

Keyloggers Characteristics:

• Keyloggers are a type of malware.

• Keyloggers are a particularly insidious type of spyware that can record and steal consecutive keystrokes (and much more) that the user enters on a device.

• The term keylogger, or "keystroke logger," is self-explanatory: Software that logs what you type on your keyboard.

• However, keyloggers can also enable cybercriminals to eavesdrop on you, watch you on your system camera, or listen over your smartphone's microphone.

• Keyloggers may be used for a number of objectives, including fraudulently gaining access to your private information and monitoring staff actions. Some keyloggers may also record your screen at random intervals; these are known as screen recorders.

• A keylogger is a malicious computer application that records everything you write on the keyboard and learns the keystroke pattern, including words, characters, and symbols, and then sends all of the recorded information to hostile hackers.

Hence the correct answer is option 1.

q: What is a common sign that a computer might be infected with a virus?
options: Unusual system slowdowns and unexpected errors
solution:
The correct answer is Unusual system slowdowns and unexpected errors.

Key Points

• One of the common symptoms of a computer virus infection is unusual system slowdowns that occur without any apparent reason.

• Unexpected errors and crashes are also indicative of a potential virus infection, disrupting normal operations.

• Infected systems may display frequent and unwanted pop-up ads, even when not browsing the internet.

• Another sign is the presence of unknown programs or processes running in the background, which were not installed by the user.

• Changes in system settings and the appearance of unfamiliar toolbars in the browser can also indicate a virus infection.

Additional Information

• Virus Definition

• A computer virus is a type of malicious software program designed to replicate itself by modifying other programs and inserting its own code.

• Viruses typically require a host program to function and spread from one computer to another.

• Common Types of Viruses

• File Infector Virus: Attaches itself to executable files and spreads when the infected file is run.

• Macro Virus: Embeds itself into documents and spreadsheets that contain macros.

• Boot Sector Virus: Infects the master boot record and is activated when the computer is started.

• Prevention Measures

• Install and regularly update antivirus software to detect and remove viruses.

• Avoid downloading and opening email attachments from unknown or untrusted sources.

• Keep your operating system and all software up to date with the latest security patches.

• Impact of Viruses

• Viruses can lead to data loss, system corruption, and unauthorized access to sensitive information.

• They can also cause significant downtime and financial losses for both individuals and organizations.

q: What is the purpose of enabling passwords on a PC?
options: For improving the data signal strength
For providing an additional layer of security
For printing of the data in the PC
solution:
The correct answer is For providing an additional layer of security.

Key Points

• Passwords help in protecting sensitive information stored on the PC by restricting access only to authorized users.

• They act as the first line of defense against unauthorized access and potential data breaches.

• Passwords help in maintaining the privacy of personal and professional data.

• Enabling passwords can prevent unauthorized changes to system settings and software configurations.

Additional Information

• Encryption

• Encryption is the process of converting data into a code to prevent unauthorized access.

• It is used to protect sensitive data both in transit and at rest.

• Common encryption methods include AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) and RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman).

• Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

• 2FA adds an extra layer of security by requiring two forms of identification before access is granted.

• This usually includes something you know (password) and something you have (mobile device for OTP).

• 2FA is widely used in online banking, email services, and secure systems.

• Biometric Authentication

• Biometric authentication uses unique biological traits such as fingerprints, retina scans, or facial recognition for identification.

• It is considered more secure than traditional passwords as biometrics are harder to replicate.

• Commonly used in smartphones, secure facilities, and high-security areas.

• Antivirus Software

• Antivirus software is designed to detect, prevent, and remove malware, including viruses, worms, and trojans.

• Regular updates are essential for antivirus software to protect against the latest threats.

• Popular antivirus programs include Norton, McAfee, and Kaspersky.
